summary: Yukteshwar Kumar is a sinologist who studied at Visva-Bharati University, Peking University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University under Tan Chung. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, the University of Delhi (~2003–2011), and the University of Bath (~2012).
Yulian Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, where she studied under Kirill Jurievitch Solonin (attested 2010).
Yumi Katayama is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied as a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

Yumi Nakamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2014) and held posts there as a public recruitment researcher in 2012 and a graduate research student in 2014.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from circa 1981 to 1989 and later held a post there around 1997.

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University in 2006. He held an assistant professorship at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, studying under Yun-shan Tan. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University (1953) and professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

Yun-shan Tan (1898–1983) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Lan-Chi Chen, Ziyuan Long, Taixu, and Kshitimohan Sen, and taught at Lida Academy and as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University.
Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Chun-fang Yu (attested 2011).

Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1937 to 1940 and later served as a professor there from circa 1965 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Tohoku University (~1945–1948). He held posts at Koyasan University (~1957–1972), Shuchiin University, and Nagoya University, where he was named Professor Emeritus in 1976.

Yusho Wakahara is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Eshō Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University (assistant professor attested 1987–1999; professor attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he was attested as Emeritus Professor in 2006.

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) worked in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Kyushu University (~1950–1954), later served as Professor Emeritus there (~1995–2013), and held a post at Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University.

Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1932–1935) under Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka. He later held posts at Soka University (~1971–1978) and Kyoto Tachibana University (~1978–1988).
Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda and held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024).

Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Kyoto University (1957–1986) and held a post at the Collège de France in 1985.

Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University from circa 1971 to 1999.

Yutaka Yoshida is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Hitotsubashi University, later holding posts at Hitotsubashi University (~1984–2006) and Kyoto University (~2006–2018).
Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957). He later served as a professor at Kanagawa University from circa 1973 to 2002.
